(4) `git diff --stat main...HEAD` confirms CLAUDE.md, README.md, and docs/migration/README.md are untouched -- only docs/requirements.yaml plus this run's own handoff/status bookkeeping files changed. (5) Deliberate-divergence grep ('unlike R-Co|deliberately diverges|diverges from R-Co') run independently against main and HEAD: 52 matches both times, content byte-identical after stripping line-number prefixes. (6) Structural scan (not count-trusting): wrote and ran a script walking every '.zig'-bearing line in the REQ-011..REQ-050 range backward to its nearest blank line or YAML unit boundary looking for the marker -- zero unmarked citation lines found; every .zig-bearing block has a PROVENANCE marker somewhere above it within the same unit. (7) `python -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"` against the current working tree's docs/requirements.yaml parses cleanly with no errors, including around every '#'-comment marker insertion. Checked docs/anti-patterns.md: no existing entry bears on this class of mechanical apply-step or on YAML-comment marking conventions specifically. SUBSTANTIVE JUDGMENT CALL (the one requiring real scrutiny, not a rubber stamp): DOC-UPDATER used a '#'-prefixed YAML comment for the marker in two contexts the design's three named unit shapes (line/paragraph/table) didn't enumerate -- above acceptance_criteria bullet items (9 instances) and above '# ---' stage-header comment blocks (3 instances, S1/S2/S3). Verdict: this is a defensible, in-scope mechanical extension of the existing single convention to a YAML syntax context the design didn't foresee, NOT a silently-invented second convention requiring CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR sign-off. Reasoning: the design's §2(c) rejected-alternative was a *stylistically different* marker per context (bold/heading in docs/ vs. an HTML- or Elixir-comment wrapper) that would have required a two-branch regex -- that is not what happened here. The marker's literal text is byte-identical in every '#'-prefixed instance; §2(a)'s regex (PROVENANCE \(historical, not current decision authority\):) still matches every one of these lines unmodified, since '#' is YAML punctuation prepended for syntactic legality, not a rewording; a bare prose line in these two positions would either corrupt acceptance_criteria's YAML sequence (becoming a spurious extra list item) or look inconsistent inside a commented-out banner block, so the '#' prefix is structurally forced, not a stylistic choice. This is the same category of reasoning the design itself already applies when noting the same literal string is legal unstyled prose in both `.md` files and `@moduledoc """..."""` heredocs (§2c) -- YAML comment syntax is a third host context the design didn't enumerate, but the same 'one literal string, no per-context styling divergence' logic extends cleanly to it without breaking constraint (a) or (b). Recommend (MINOR, non-blocking) that REQ-237's design doc be amended to explicitly enumerate the YAML-comment-line case as a fourth citation-unit shape, since three more sibling chunks (255/256/257) will hit docs/requirements.yaml's same acceptance_criteria/stage-header contexts and should not each have to re-derive this same judgment independently.
